audit: Independent raw-output review of all paired verifier-model comparison results
method: Read raw response message text, not RESULTS.md, summaries or stored assessments, to adjudicate every main and choice explanation. Replay strict native adaptation offline, compare exact requests to plan and paired requests excluding modelId, verify historical item/solution identity except predeclared local index. No provider calls, source edits, output repairs or relabeling.

feedback.text: When a conjunctive adverb like 'however' links two independent clauses, a semicolon must precede it and a comma must follow it.
feedback.reason: Treats one conventional however placement as mandatory and does not allow however to attach to the first clause.

feedback.choice: The conference ended at noon, many attendees stayed for the workshop.
feedback.text: Two independent clauses joined only by a comma is a comma splice; no semicolon is used at all.
feedback.reason: The comma-splice choice has no semicolon and does not answer the question.

feedback.choice: The conference ended at noon; however, many attendees stayed for the workshop.
feedback.text: A semicolon before the conjunctive adverb 'however' and a comma after it is the standard correct form for joining two independent clauses.
feedback.reason: This is a conventional valid semicolon/conjunctive-adverb pattern; its validity does not establish uniqueness.

feedback.choice: The conference ended at noon, however; many attendees stayed for the workshop.
feedback.text: The semicolon is misplaced after 'however' instead of before it, violating the rule for conjunctive adverbs.
feedback.reason: The comma-however-semicolon construction is defensible with however attached to the first independent clause; the claimed mandatory preceding semicolon is false.

feedback.choice: The conference ended at noon; and many attendees stayed for the workshop.
feedback.text: Placing a semicolon before the coordinating conjunction 'and' is nonstandard; a comma before 'and' is the correct form.
feedback.reason: A comma before and is the ordinary recommendation here, but the blanket nonstandard characterization is style-sensitive. This additional uncertainty is not needed for the independently established multiple-defensible-answer failure.

primary_grammar_source.location: Printed page 5, R2 and the first-clause however example
primary_grammar_source.supports: The comma-however-semicolon construction can be valid; the model explanations incorrectly make one placement mandatory.

conclusion: Both arms fail the frozen component qualification: each accepts both known defective items and repeats the false paint ratio. Both also write false exclusions of the rounded 13% distractor. Opus has sound weighted-average feedback; Sonnet names swapping as a possible source of 79.2 even though swapped weights yield 81.6, recorded as material uncertainty and failure. This selected six-case run does not qualify either model or establish broad superiority.
limitations: All questions are selected reused diagnostics, not unseen holdouts.
There were no negative reviews, so neither arm demonstrated rejection of either known bad control; no defect-specific rejection rationale is observable.
Full-content pass counts concern decision/key/teaching; both fuel reviews also underrate direct-application difficulty as 1, recorded separately.
A schema-valid, bounded review can still accept a nonunique item or give false feedback. No transport or parser defect accounts for these observed content errors.
